coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 9 unit directories containing an *-index.md (the domain root plus 17.01, 17.02, 17.03, 17.05, 17.08, 17.09, 17.10, 17.11) and 55 markdown files — exactly matching the expected 9 units / 55 files. All 55 files were read in full; no sampling. 17.04, 17.06, 17.07, 17.12, 17.13 and 17.14 are leaf feature files of the domain root unit (six root-level features, per the domain index's '8 sub-domains + 6 features'), and 17.08.03 was read as part of the 17.08 unit. Leaf-count check passes: 6 root features + 31 sub-domain leaves = 37, matching the domain index D-02 claim. Checkpoints scored per file (5 applicable vision dimensions x file count); dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A throughout, because personas, constraints and competitive landscape are authored once in meta/ and referenced — never redefined — in every unit of this domain. Two systematic sweeps were run programmatically over all 55 files to verify ID-integrity findings: duplicate local D-NN/Q-NN ids in Decisions/Open Questions tables, D-NN self-cites absent from a file's own Decisions table, index-vs-header status mismatches, and [PENDING] markers whose only deferral target is a completed pipeline stage (36 such markers domain-wide, 4 of which point at questions since marked RESOLVED). Devil's-advocate pass dropped 8 candidate findings: the deposit-gates-announce conflict (tracked, 17.01.04 Q-01), per-show-vs-run settlement finality (tracked, domain Q-02), hold-ladder ownership 16 vs 17 (tracked, 17.01.01 Q-03), the free-text block-vs-warn framing (functionally identical), the 17.02 index Role Matrix wording vs 17.02.01 DT-09 (DT-09 states it sharpens rather than contradicts), sub-domain index [BREADTH] markers (process metadata), the 17.01 CX challenge-window summary '(24-48h)' (leaf file is unambiguous and authoritative), and cross-domain directory-name variants in link targets (documentation defect, not product ambiguity).

findings.claim: Silent contradiction: 17.09.01 refuses any signature against an Incomplete sheet (its central forcing function), while 17.09.05 makes a signature available on the same Incomplete sheet with an acknowledgement. Neither statement carries a marker, and 17.09.05's only nod to the conflict points at a question that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: 17.09.01-settlement-sheet-computation.md:85-86 — '5. **Signature is refused against an Incomplete sheet** (17.09.05 binds a signature to a computation; an Incomplete sheet has no complete computation to bind to). This is not a blocker ... it is a forcing function'. Same file:149 (edge case) — 'sheet state **Incomplete**; total renders as `£8,400 + 1 un-agreed term`; signature refused until both parties attest an amount or mark it not-applicable'; :180 (States, Incomplete) — 'Signature refused'; :240 (D-05) — 'the sheet is Incomplete and unsignable until then'. CONTRADICTED BY 17.09.05-settlement-signoff-variance.md:228 (edge case) — '**Deal contains free-text terms outside the grammar** (17.09.01 Q-03) | The computation is silently incomplete ... | The sheet is marked `Incomplete` and signature is available only with an explicit acknowledgement that unmodelled terms exist and are not in the arithmetic'; and :267 (Surface state Partial) — 'or unmodellable free-text terms exist | ... Signature remains available with explicit acknowledgement; the gap is never hidden to make the page look finished'. 17.09.05:289 acknowledges only 'a **live tension**: this feature must not render a complete-looking sheet over 17.09.01's `Incomplete` state (its Q-03)' — but 17.09.01's Q-03 is now 'When a settlement computes **negative** ... does the platform collect' (17.09.01:261), and its former free-text Q-03 was closed by D-05, so the pointer resolves to nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A deal carries one un-evaluated free-text term ('plus £500 if it sells out'). Implementer A builds 17.09.01 D-05: the sign action is disabled until both parties counter-attest an amount or mark the term not-applicable, so the £500 is always raised in the room. Implementer B builds 17.09.05's row: the sheet renders Incomplete, the tour manager taps an acknowledgement checkbox at 1am, both parties sign, the money moves, and the £500 is never resolved — exactly the 'confident lie' D-05 was written to make impossible. Both implementations are faithful to a ratified decision in the sub-domain, and the two produce different settled numbers on the same show.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an Incomplete settlement sheet is signable at all — i.e. whether 17.09.01 D-05's forcing function exists.

findings.claim: Silent contradiction: 17.01.03 D-14 ratifies that confirming under challenge stays available *without agreed terms*, while 17.01.04 C-01 makes an accepted offer version a hard confirmation precondition with no override 'by any party, ever'. The cross-reference that was supposed to reconcile them points at a question that has since been resolved as something else.
findings.evidence: 17.01.03-challenge-release-expiry.md:228 (D-14) — 'Confirm under challenge stays available **without agreed terms** — disclosed and recorded, not blocked | Recommendation resolving Q-01's default. Blocking drives the deal off-platform ... the industry genuinely confirms-then-papers.' Its Q-01 (:237) narrows only to 'may an Operator opt into a stricter room policy ... **Same question as 17.01.04 Q-03, asked from the other end; answer once.**' CONTRADICTED BY 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:55 — 'C-01 through C-05 have no override of any kind, by any party, ever'; :59 (C-01) — 'An **accepted offer version** exists ([17.02]) | Resolves Q-03: *confirmed* means terms agreed ... | Blocked; routes to the open offer thread'; :192 (edge case) — 'Party confirms defensively under a 48h challenge ... C-01 requires an accepted offer, so the defensive confirm at least has terms'; :274 (D-07) — 'Confirmation requires an **accepted offer version**, not an executed contract'. The reconciliation pointer is broken: 17.01.04's Q-03 (:292) now reads '~~Is a party owed anything beyond first refusal when a confirm-then-revert destroyed their hold?~~ **RESOLVED — no.**', a different question entirely.
findings.failure_scenario: 1st hold is challenged with a 48h clock and has no accepted offer version on the thread. Implementer A follows 17.01.04 C-01 and hard-blocks the confirm, so the holder drops and loses the date — the outcome 17.01.03 D-14 explicitly says drives the deal off-platform. Implementer B follows D-14 and permits the confirm with a disclosure, which destroys every inferior hold irreversibly (17.01.04 CX-03) against terms nobody agreed — the exact defensive-confirm collapse 17.01.03 DT-02 identifies. The two builds disagree on the most irreversible write in the domain, and no marker anywhere flags that the two ratified decisions conflict.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an accepted offer version is genuinely mandatory at confirm, or waived while a challenge clock is live.

findings.claim: The domain CX file asserts a confirmation precondition that appears in no precondition table and that 17.14's own happy path contradicts: that a bill with both headline and support slots cannot confirm until both slot ladders resolve.
findings.evidence: live-booking-settlement-cx.md:533-535 (CX-19 synthesis 2) — 'Publish avail with bill shape → 17.14 defines slots → each slot gets its own ladder → holds join the ladder for their slot. Confirmation requires *both* ladders resolved where a bill has support and headline (D-04) — a nuance the happy path did not state.' CONTRADICTED BY 17.14-bill-construction-support-slots.md:46-49 (Happy Path) — '1. Headline deal confirms (17.01.04). 2. The party who controls the slot — per the deal — proposes a support act.'; and :74 (States) — 'Headliner only | Main deal confirmed | Bill with open slots and who controls each'. 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:57-64 enumerates the complete precondition set C-01..C-06 ('**Confirmation preconditions** — all hard, evaluated at the moment of commit') and carries no bill or slot-ladder row; the bill precondition it does carry is P-04, which is an *announce* precondition and is satisfied by marking a slot TBA (:93). The cited '(D-04)' is 17.01.02 D-05/D-04, which concerns the room-side and artist-side ladders — 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:251 — not headline-versus-support ladders, which that file's D-05 (:252) says 'never contend and never share a ladder'.
findings.failure_scenario: A promoter confirms a headliner on a room whose avail declares a support slot. Implementer A reads CX-19 and blocks the headline confirm until the support slot's ladder also resolves, so no bill can ever confirm its headliner first — making 17.14's entire happy path (headline confirms, then supports are proposed) unreachable. Implementer B reads C-01..C-06 as exhaustive and confirms the headliner immediately. The two produce incompatible booking flows on the majority of shows (17.14 DT-01: 'most shows have two or three acts on separate deals').
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an unresolved support-slot ladder is a hard precondition of headline confirmation.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file states as fact that confirmation blocks adjacent dates through routing buffers, which two ratified decisions in the same sub-domain directly forbid; its synthesis block is still marked PENDING against a stage the leaf file says already resolved it.
findings.evidence: 17.01-availability-holds-confirmation-cx.md:112-114 (CX-04) — 'Confirmation is the only transition that hard-writes the calendar. **It also blocks adjacent dates via travel/routing windows, which is why a confirmed London date can make a Glasgow date the next night unbookable.**'; and :121-122 — '**Synthesis questions answered**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — the routing buffer rule is owned by domain 18 (Touring) and cannot be specified from inside 17.' CONTRADICTED BY 17.01.01-availability-calendar-avails.md:292 (D-14) — '**Routing buffers annotate an avail; they never block it** ... A buffer that auto-blocks decides a routing question on evidence the platform does not have. **Resolves breadth-pass Q-03 and CX-04's PENDING** (DT-13)'; and 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:71 (W-02, under 'Confirmation warnings — surfaced, never blocking') — 'Travel infeasible against an adjacent confirmed date | The routing/buffer rule is owned by domain 18 and cannot be authored from inside 17'.
findings.failure_scenario: An artist confirms London on 14 March. Implementer A follows CX-04 and writes a hard block onto the next night's Glasgow avail, so the agent cannot even take a hold on a date the act was willing to fly to — the outcome 17.01.01 DT-13 rejects on domain 18's ratified position. Implementer B follows D-14 and renders the date annotated 'tight' with 18.11.02's arithmetic attached. One build silently removes sellable inventory the artist never agreed to give up.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a routing buffer written at confirmation removes an adjacent date from the avails surface.

findings.claim: Two files in the same unit decompose a two-stage venue incompatibly — one says two stages are two rooms with two calendars, the other says one room with two stages has several slots — and the sub-domain index's resolution of Q-01 sides with the second.
findings.evidence: 17.01.01-availability-calendar-avails.md:60-62 — 'This resolves the sub-domain's Q-01 from the avail side: a room with a matinee and an evening publishes **two** avails over two intervals; **a venue with two stages has two rooms** (16.01.02) with two calendars and therefore two independent avails. No new grain is invented here.' (restated at :281, D-03 — 'matinee + evening = two intervals; two stages = two rooms (16.01.02)'). CONTRADICTED BY 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:51-54 — '**The ladder's unit is a slot, not a date** (D-05). One room-date is one slot *by default*, but **a room with two stages**, a matinee plus an evening, or a headline plus two support positions **has several**'; and 17.01-availability-holds-confirmation-index.md:59 (Q-01 resolution) — 'Default: one room-date = one slot; **the Operator declares more when the room has more (two stages, matinee + evening, headline vs support)**'. 17.01.02:229 flags the seam without resolving it: 'Reconciliation needed at Step 6: 17.01.01's avail is a "window with constraints" and this feature's unit is a slot (D-05); the two must agree that a window decomposes into slots' — and Step 6 is complete per live-booking-settlement-cx.md:12.
findings.failure_scenario: A two-stage venue onboards. Implementer A follows 17.01.01 D-03 and models it as two rooms in domain 16, each with one slot per date, so a hold on the main stage cannot even be expressed as a slot within a room. Implementer B follows 17.01.02 D-05 and the index's Q-01 resolution and models one room with two Operator-declared slots. Contention, ladder identity, C-05's same-date double-book block and D-12's cross-room void prompt all evaluate against different keys in the two builds, so a matinee-plus-evening double-header is legal in one and hard-blocked in the other.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether stage decomposition lives at domain 16's room level or at 17's slot level.

findings.claim: 17.01.02 assigns the identifier D-14 to two different ratified decisions in one Decisions table, so every citation of '17.01.02 D-14' is ambiguous.
findings.evidence: 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:260 — '| D-14 | **DQ-04.01:** a held date **stays available**, and only an **aggregate** hold state is disclosed — never counterparty identities | ...'; and :262 — '| D-14 | **Requests lapse; holds expire.** Different objects, different clocks. A lapse closes as `no-response`, never as `declined` | DT-14. Resolves old Q-03. ... Default 7 days, Operator-configurable 1–30, warned at day 5.' The rows are also out of sequence (D-14, D-13, D-14, D-15). The collision is load-bearing across files: 17.07-booking-enquiry-inbox-rfq.md:138 resolves its Q-01 by citing '`17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md` **D-14**' and quoting the lapse decision. Programmatic sweep over all 55 files found this and one other duplicate-id case, and no others.
findings.failure_scenario: A spec writer implementing enquiry lapse resolves the citation '17.01.02 D-14' and lands on the availability-disclosure decision instead of the lapse decision, or vice versa — the two govern entirely unrelated behaviour (what a counterparty may see about contention, versus the 7-day request clock and the `no-response` close reason). The propagate-decision and write-be-spec stages both resolve decisions by id.
findings.forcedInvention: Which decision the identifier 17.01.02 D-14 denotes.

findings.claim: 17.02.03 states two decisions, D-07 and D-08, as its own ratified rulings and is cited for them from a sibling file, but its Decisions table defines only D-01 through D-06 — so both decisions have no authored row anywhere.
findings.evidence: 17.02.03-offer-approval-chain.md Decisions table (:112-117) contains exactly D-01..D-06. The file nonetheless states: :70 — '| Offer expires mid-approval | **DQ-04.03 (D-08):** the offer expires. There is **no implicit grace window** ...'; :71 — '| Band has never configured a rule | **DQ-04.02 (D-07):** this feature does not invent one.'; :72 — '**Resolved (Q-01 / D-03, D-07, D-08).**'; :123 (Q-01 resolution) — 'Source: **this file's D-07** (Edge Cases → "Band has never configured a rule")'; :124 (Q-02 resolution) — 'Source: **this file's D-08** (Edge Cases → "Offer expires mid-approval")'; :125 (Q-03) — '**Per DQ-04.03 / D-08** — does an extension re-open the hold ladder clock?'. findings.failure_scenario: A downstream spec writer resolving '17.02.03 D-08' for the no-grace-window rule finds no such decision and must either invent the rule or treat it as unratified — while 17.02.04's Q-01 and Q-02 both declare themselves RESOLVED on the strength of it, so the expiry-versus-approval race is recorded as settled by a decision that does not exist as a decision.

findings.claim: 17.02.03 has two different open questions both numbered Q-03, and an edge case defers to '[PENDING — Q-03]' without saying which.

The ambiguity is consumed at :73 — '| Member approves, then the band's lineup changes before the show | `[PENDING — Q-03 → /write-architecture-spec]` | — |', which resolves correctly only by matching the deferral target rather than the id. Both govern whether a recorded entity approval still binds.

findings.claim: The same economic-content detector is specified twice with materially different trigger conditions — 17.02.01 requires a money keyword within 40 characters of a number, 17.03.01 fires on a money keyword alone — and the two keyword lists differ. Neither marks the divergence.
findings.evidence: 17.02.01-offer-sheet-composition.md:68 (the lint table, ratified at D-06 :235) — 'Free text carries an **economic signal** with no structured counterpart — a currency symbol or ISO code adjacent to a number (`£500`, `EUR 750`); **a number followed by `%`; an economic noun/verb within 40 characters of a number** (`pay, plus, bonus, deduct, cut, fee, split, extra, additional, waive, cover, reimburse, per head, per ticket, comp`); a conditional near a number (`if`, `once`, `provided`, `subject to`, `in the event`) | **Warn and require acknowledgment**'. 17.03.01-deal-term-grammar-types.md:172 (ratified at D-09 :274) — 'Detector fires at send: **any free text containing a currency symbol, a number adjacent to `%`, or a money keyword** (`fee`, `bonus`, `pay`, `cut`, `deduct`, `plus`, `less`, `owed`, `split`, `guarantee`) **blocks the send**'. The second has no number-proximity requirement at all and adds `less`, `owed`, `guarantee`; the first adds `waive`, `cover`, `reimburse`, `per head`, `per ticket`, `comp`. 17.03.01:244 assigns the mechanism to the sibling — 'The economic-content detector (D-09) fires **at that feature's send action**' — without noting that the two files state different trigger conditions.
findings.failure_scenario: An Operator types the bespoke term 'no support act may use the house kit; hospitality is on a fee-free basis'. Under 17.03.01 D-09 the bare keyword `fee` fires the detector and the send is blocked pending an acknowledgement recorded on the offer and carried onto the settlement sheet. Under 17.02.01 D-06 no number is adjacent, nothing fires, and the offer sends clean. The two builds produce different sets of acknowledged un-evaluated terms, which is the exact quantity 17.09.01 D-06 nominates as 'the grammar's honest, per-settlement ceiling measurement' for deciding domain Q-08.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a money keyword with no adjacent number fires the economic-content detector.

findings.claim: 17.13's `Meaningful` state is gated on 'a threshold' that is never given a value or a basis, and no open question in the file or the domain covers it — unlike every comparable threshold elsewhere in the domain, which is either numbered or explicitly tracked.
findings.evidence: 17.13-fan-demand-signals.md:66 (States) — '| Meaningful | Signals above a threshold in a market | Aggregate count with its confidence |'; :65 — '| Accumulating | Signals arriving | Demand map with low confidence |'. The file's three open questions (:102-104) cover whether a Fan touchpoint is wanted at all (Q-01), brigading (Q-02) and request-to-attendance conversion (Q-03); none mentions the threshold, and the domain index's Q-05 (live-booking-settlement-index.md:137) mirrors only Q-01. Contrast the domain's own treatment of the same class of number: 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:277 (Q-07) — '**Three platform-default numbers are set here on reasoning, not on observed industry practice, and want owner ratification**: request lapse 7 days ...; stale threshold 30 days; flapping threshold 3-in-30-days'; 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:295 (Q-06) — '**What is the announce-runway warning threshold, and where does it come from?** The interim default above (28 days) is a **stated starting value, not a researched constant**'; 17.11.01-verified-draw-record.md:69 — 'Enough shows in a market to be a fact (threshold `[PENDING — Step 5 Must-depth or /write-be-spec]`)'.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must invent both the number and its basis — 500 raw requests, or 2% of a market's population, or a proportion of the artist's followers there — and the choice decides when a demand signal becomes visible to an Operator beside a hold request (17.13 Role Lens: 'Reads aggregate demand for an act when deciding a hold'). A low absolute threshold makes every small city 'meaningful' and reduces the signal to noise; a high one makes the feature permanently empty outside major markets. Two implementers reading independently produce different products, and D-02's 'never rendered as a forecast' constraint does not bound either.
findings.forcedInvention: The value and the basis of the threshold at which a market's demand signals become `Meaningful`.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table records a depth status for four children that contradicts those files' own headers, and the index's own status marker contradicts its CX file's.
findings.evidence: live-booking-settlement-index.md:55, 58, 63, 65 list 17.04, 17.07, 17.12 and 17.14 as `[SURFACE]`. The files themselves: 17.04-performance-contracts-deal-memos.md:5 — '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'; 17.07-booking-enquiry-inbox-rfq.md:5 — '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'; 17.12-counterparty-relationship-payment-reliability.md:5 — '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'; 17.14-bill-construction-support-slots.md:5 — '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'. findings.failure_scenario: A downstream stage (remediate-pipeline, plan-phase, or a subsequent audit scoping pass) selects work by depth marker, reads the domain index as the pipeline key file per its own convention, and treats four `[PARTIAL]` features — including 17.14 Bill Construction, which the domain's own D-10 calls a correction to 'an assumption wrong on the majority of shows' — as undeepened `[SURFACE]` stubs needing a discovery pass they have already had, or conversely skips them as out of scope for depth-gated work.
findings.forcedInvention: The actual deepening status of 17.04, 17.07, 17.12 and 17.14.

Also stage-only and unowned: 17.10.03:64 and :65 — '`[PENDING — Step 5]`'; 17.10.02-disbursement-execution.md:73 — 'Enforcement mechanics `[PENDING — Step 5 Must-depth]`'; 17.10-live-income-payout-tax-cx.md:71 — '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' and :92 — '5. **State transition conflict**: `[PENDING — Step 5]`.'
findings.failure_scenario: A spec writer reads 17.10.03's VAT edge case, sees `[PENDING — Step 5]`, and scopes VAT-on-fee work into this feature — directly against D-03 and the resolved Q-03, which place VAT wholly in domain 23. The unresolved marker outranks the resolution in the reader's eye because it sits in the behavioural table rather than the questions table, and it names no owner who could adjudicate.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether VAT-on-fee and reduced-rate prompting remain open in this feature, and who owns them if so.

Usually yes; not always | `[PENDING — Step 5]` |' (this one names no question at all); :105 — '| Radius measured how — driving distance or straight line? | ... | `[PENDING — Step 5]` — a real, unglamorous specification gap |'. 17.04-performance-contracts-deal-memos.md:66 — 'the deep case (signer lost authority mid-flight) is `[PENDING — Step 5]`'. 17.13-fan-demand-signals.md:53 — '| Signals gamed — an artist's fans brigade a city | ... | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — a signal that can be manufactured is a signal (Q-02) |'. The stage is complete (live-booking-settlement-cx.md:12, 'The Step-6 pass ... completed the synthesis the breadth pass deferred'), so none of these has a stage that will resolve it; 17.06:102 and 17.04:66 additionally name no question and no owner.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the radius check reaches 'Clause on a show that is later cancelled' and finds a marker with no owner, no question row, and a deferral target that has already run. They must invent whether a live radius clause survives the cancellation of the show it protects — which determines whether an artist's calendar stays constrained by a show that no longer exists. The same applies to whether a signer who loses authority mid-flight can complete a contract execution (17.04:66), a permission question with legal force.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a radius clause survives its protecting show's cancellation, and whether a signer who loses authority mid-execution may complete the signature.
